- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.5) and understate when sentiment is negative (especially <0.3).  
- Model tends to lag behind true price movements, especially after sharp spikes — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for prices rising >5% in recent history.  
- Overshoots after strong sentiment-driven rallies — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below true peak if sentiment was high and price surged.  
- Mean-reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often undercorrects — add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price if sentiment is volatile or mixed — increase forecast by 1–3% if sentiment variance >0.3.  
- Avoid overreacting to recent low sentiment — if sentiment drops below 0.2, don’t assume price will fall; instead, forecast slightly higher to avoid underestimating rebound.
